These movements, often led by scholars and Sufi mystics, emphasized the importance of seeking knowledge and striving for personal growth. The term Nahzat came to symbolize a sense of restlessness or agitation that drove individuals to seek out new ideas and perspectives, leading to intellectual and spiritual advancements within the Islamic community.

The feeling of Nahzat can be seen as a call from within, urging individuals to investigate the mysteries of the universe and abandon complacency or stagnation in their search for truth. By embracing the feeling of Nahzat, individuals can deepen their connection to God and continue their spiritual journey towards self-improvement and enlightenment.
